symbols.name: G
symbols.def: Supplied labeled process DAG whose cross-variable arrows respect the order on \(V\).

symbols.name: u
symbols.def: Source of the queried direct transfer.

symbols.name: v
symbols.def: Target of the queried direct transfer, with \(u<v\).

symbols.name: L
symbols.def: Uniform entry bound for the fine transition.

symbols.name: d_min
symbols.def: Lower eigenvalue bound for the fine innovation covariance.

symbols.name: d_max
symbols.def: Upper eigenvalue bound for the fine innovation covariance.

symbols.name: kappa
symbols.def: Separation margin for nonzero divided differences and regular branches.

symbols.name: N
symbols.def: Precision index for rational outward rounding.

symbols.name: n
symbols.def: Number of observed coarse transitions in \((Y_0,\ldots,Y_n)\).

symbols.name: Rm
symbols.def: Sum of monomials in \((A^m)_{vu}\) indexed by nondecreasing walks from \(u\) to \(v\) containing at least two strict increases.

symbols.name: K
symbols.def: Ordered field with effective arithmetic, sign tests, and real-root isolation; \(\mathbb Q\) and \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\) are admissible.

symbols.name: Zeval
symbols.def: Prespecified finite frequency grid for simultaneous Wald bands.

symbols.name: hatB
symbols.def: \(\widehat B=\widehat M_1\widehat M_0^{-1}\) whenever \(\widehat M_0\) is positive definite.

symbols.name: hath
symbols.def: Regular-branch plug-in transfer obtained by graph recursion from \((\widehat B,\widehat Q)\) and evaluation of \(A_{vu}z/(1-A_{vv}z)\).

symbols.name: Sigmah
symbols.def: Long-run delta-method covariance of the stacked real and imaginary parts of \((\widehat h_{uv}(z))_{z\in\mathcal Z}\).

symbols.name: Hell
symbols.def: Matrices \(H_{\ell ij}\) satisfying \(W_n^\top H_{0ij}W_n=(\widehat M_0)_{ij}\) and \(W_n^\top H_{1ij}W_n=(\widehat M_1)_{ij}\).

symbols.name: Ksigma
symbols.def: Explicit uniform bound \(K_\Sigma=d_{\max}\sum_{r=0}^{m-1}(dL)^{2r}\left[\{1-(1-\gamma)^m\}^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{d-1}\{2(dL)^m/(1-(1-\gamma)^m)\}^k\right]^2\) on \(\|\operatorname{Cov}(W_n)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\), obtained through the coarse spectral-density resolvent.

symbols.name: OutN
symbols.def: A verified interval-arithmetic operator returning a rational interval containing \([x-r,x+r]\).

symbols.name: Rinverse
symbols.def: Fine-model inverse \(\mathcal R_n\) of \(\mathcal C_n^M(\alpha)\) through the stationary moment equations, restricted to the compact ordered process-DAG class.

symbols.name: Cert
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{Cert}_{uv,m,G}(B,Q)\) enumerates real diagonal root branches, eliminates every nonsingular off-diagonal coordinate by the triangular divided-difference recursion, invokes exact CAD on each residual singular system and its two-copy transfer-inequality system, and returns either incompatibility, the common rational transfer, or two exact stable transfer-distinct witnesses.

symbols.name: CalHandle
symbols.def: Build a data-adaptive calibration by splitting each centered lag-moment quadratic form into positive and negative spectral parts, upper-bounding their trace and operator norms with a confidence envelope for the block-Toeplitz trajectory covariance, and applying verified rational interval arithmetic before semialgebraic inversion; the calibration itself is to be derived.

assumptions.condition: Every cross-variable arrow \(i\to j\) in \(G\) satisfies \(i<j\).

novel.justification: An externally fixed order is realistic for layered physical, biological, and production systems in which upstream and downstream variables are determined before time-series fitting; the assumption is maintained rather than inferred from the Gaussian law.

assumptions.condition: The queried arrow \(u\to v\) belongs to \(G\).
\(A_{ij}=0\) for every \(i>j\) such that \(j\to i\notin G\).
The sequence \((\varepsilon_t)_{t\in\mathbb Z}\) is independent and identically distributed as \(N(0,D)\).

standard.name: uniform stability margin for a triangular VAR

novel.justification: The excluded collision sets are algebraic hypersurfaces; persistence coefficients bounded away from simultaneous zero or opposite-sign collision describe a nondegenerate region that is stable under small perturbations.

assumptions.condition: Every entry of \(B\) and \(Q\) is represented in the effective real closed field \(K\).

novel.justification: Rational and real-algebraic population inputs, as well as verified rational enclosures of digital sample moments, have exactly this representation; the condition distinguishes an executable certificate from a merely set-theoretic definability claim.

definitions.name: compatible fine-grid fiber
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal S(B,Q;G)=\{(A,D):A^m=B,\ \sum_{r=0}^{m-1}A^rD(A^r)^\top=Q,\ A_{ij}=0\text{ for }i<j,\ A_{ij}=0\text{ for }i>j\text{ with }j\to i\notin G,\ \max_i|A_{ii}|<1,\ D_{ij}=0\text{ for }i\ne j,\ D\succ0\}\).

definitions.name: graph-recursive root map
definitions.construction: For each selected real diagonal root \(A_{ii}\) of \(B_{ii}\), process pairs \((v,u)\) in increasing \(v-u\); when \(C_m(A_{vv},A_{uu})\ne0\), set \(A_{vu}=\{B_{vu}-R_{vu,m}(A)\}/C_m(A_{vv},A_{uu})\) on an allowed edge and set forbidden entries to zero subject to their induced compatibility equations.

definitions.name: formula-or-ambiguity certificate
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{Cert}_{uv,m,G}(B,Q)\) is the exact algorithm declared by symbol \(\mathrm{Cert}\), using the graph-recursive root map on regular coordinates and CAD on the remaining semialgebraic fiber and two-copy transfer comparison.

definitions.name: branch-free semialgebraic inverse
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal R_n=\{(A,D):\exists(M_0,M_1)\in\mathcal C_n^M(\alpha),\ M_0\succ0,\ M_1=A^mM_0,\ M_0=A^mM_0(A^m)^\top+\sum_{r=0}^{m-1}A^rD(A^r)^\top,\ A_{ij}=0\text{ for }i<j,\ A_{ij}=0\text{ for }i>j\text{ with }j\to i\notin G,\ \max_i|A_{ii}|\le1-\gamma,\ \max_{i,j}|A_{ij}|\le L,\ D_{ij}=0\text{ for }i\ne j,\ d_{\min}I_d\preceq D\preceq d_{\max}I_d\}\).

definitions.name: regular recursive plug-in estimator
definitions.construction: Compute \((\widehat B,\widehat Q)\) from \((\widehat M_0,\widehat M_1)\), apply the unique odd graph-recursive root map, recover diagonal \(D\) recursively, and set \(\widehat h_{uv}(z)=\widehat A_{vu}z/(1-\widehat A_{vv}z)\) for \(z\in\mathcal Z\).

definitions.name: spectral-split adaptive calibration handle
definitions.construction: Use \(\mathrm{CalHandle}\): spectral splitting of the stacked lag quadratic forms, a data-dependent block-Toeplitz covariance envelope, and verified rational outward rounding targeted at a coordinatewise smaller moment box whose full semialgebraic inverse remains uniformly valid.

statements.statement: The observed process satisfies \(Y_s=BY_{s-1}+\eta_s\), where \(B=A^m\), \(\eta_s\) is independent Gaussian white noise with covariance \(Q\), and \(B=M_1M_0^{-1}\), \(Q=M_0-BM_0B^\top\). Conversely, stable \(B\) and positive definite \(Q\) determine the stationary coarse Gaussian law.
statements.justification: This reduces observational equivalence to two coarse matrices before any root argument.
statements.gap: Gong et al. derive the subsampled transition and innovation mixture; the converse coarse-law sufficiency is recorded here to fix the exact fiber.
statements.consumer: The certificate and both inference procedures use \((B,Q)\) or equivalently \((M_0,M_1)\) as their complete observed-law input.

statements.statement: For every \(u<v\), \((A^m)_{vu}=A_{vu}C_m(A_{vv},A_{uu})+R_{vu,m}(A)\), and each monomial of \(R_{vu,m}(A)\) follows a directed path from \(u\) to \(v\) with at least two strict vertex increases and only smaller endpoint gaps.
statements.justification: The identity exposes the exact coefficient whose vanishing separates recursive identification from singular fibers.
statements.gap: Smith's triangular recurrence is numerical and branch-oriented; the graph-indexed path remainder and its causal support checks are the adapted algebraic form.
statements.consumer: It lets a scientist recover a queried edge without solving the full matrix polynomial whenever the ancestral recursion is regular.

statements.statement: If \(m\) is odd, then \(C_m(x,y)>0\) for every \((x,y)\ne(0,0)\) and \(C_m(0,0)=0\). If \(m\) is even, then \(C_m(x,y)=0\) if and only if \(x=-y\).
statements.justification: The zero set supplies the sharp parity-specific collision geometry.
statements.gap: Classical root algorithms note singular recurrences but do not translate their zero locus into a causal identification frontier.
statements.consumer: It tells a data analyst which persistence configurations require the exact fallback rather than the closed-form recursion.

statements.statement: Suppose \(m\) is odd and no allowed edge \(j\to i\) has \(A_{ii}=A_{jj}=0\). Then every nonempty \(\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\) is a singleton. Its diagonal is \(A_{ii}=B_{ii}^{1/m}\); its allowed off-diagonal entries are recovered in increasing endpoint gap by \(A_{ij}=\{B_{ij}-R_{ij,m}(A)\}/C_m(A_{ii},A_{jj})\); and its diagonal innovations are recovered in increasing \(i\) by \(D_{ii}=\{Q_{ii}-\sum_{j<i}D_{jj}\sum_{r=0}^{m-1}(A^r)_{ij}^2\}/\sum_{r=0}^{m-1}A_{ii}^{2r}\). Full substitution into forbidden entries and off-diagonal covariance equations is necessary and sufficient for compatibility. Consequently \(\mathcal H_{uv}(B,Q;G)=\{h_{uv}\}\).
statements.justification: This is the constructive point-identification half of the parity frontier.
statements.gap: Gong et al. require non-Gaussian shocks for recovery; Smith computes a chosen root but does not prove uniqueness after graph and innovation-covariance checks.
statements.consumer: Fine-grid policy or scientific impulse analysis can use a closed-form transfer even though only every \(m\)-th state was recorded.

statements.statement: If \(m\) is even and \((A,D)\in\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\), then \((-A,D)\in\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\). If \(A_{vu}\ne0\), the two attained transfers \(A_{vu}z/(1-A_{vv}z)\) and \(-A_{vu}z/(1+A_{vv}z)\) are unequal as rational functions. Hence no nonzero queried edge transfer is point identified from the Gaussian coarse law under an even factor.
statements.justification: The global sign action is an unavoidable same-law obstruction that covariance filtering cannot remove.
statements.gap: Gong et al.'s even sign conclusion is embedded in a non-Gaussian identification theorem; this claim proves the obstruction directly for the Gaussian law after the complete coarse covariance restriction.
statements.consumer: For a conditionally ordered Temperature--Ozone analysis with \(m=2\), the result prevents reporting a branch-selected directional transfer as identified.

statements.statement: Under effective \(K\)-valued inputs, \(\operatorname{Cert}_{uv,m,G}(B,Q)\) terminates and is sound and complete. It returns incompatibility exactly when \(\mathcal S(B,Q;G)=\varnothing\); it returns one rational function exactly when every element of \(\mathcal H_{uv}(B,Q;G)\) is equal; otherwise it returns two attained stable pairs \((A,D),(A',D')\in\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\) satisfying \((A_{vu}-A'_{vu})^2+(A_{vu}A'_{vv}-A'_{vu}A_{vv})^2>0\). The certificate remains complete for zero diagonals, zero queried edges, open fibers, positive-dimensional fibers, and branch mergers.
statements.justification: A total formula-or-ambiguity output replaces numerical root selection by an auditable causal identification certificate.
statements.gap: Classical CAD decides semialgebraic formulas and classical root methods select branches; neither provides this target-aware graph-recursive contract with covariance filtering and exact transfer-distinct witnesses.
statements.consumer: Software for subsampled process-DAG analysis can refuse false singleton answers and furnish two explicit observationally equivalent causal explanations when identification fails.

statements.statement: For \(d=2\), \(m=3\), \(B=0\), and \(Q=\operatorname{diag}(q_1,q_2)\succ0\), the matrices \(A=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&0\\a&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)\) and \(D=\operatorname{diag}(q_1,q_2-a^2q_1)\) belong to the compatible fiber for every \(|a|<\sqrt{q_2/q_1}\). Thus a queried lower edge has an open interval of attained transfer coefficients, and the certificate must return two interior witnesses rather than unattained endpoints.
statements.justification: This is the destructive sanity check for singular odd-factor completeness.
statements.gap: A regular-root recursion alone would incorrectly suggest odd-factor point identification at this collision.
statements.consumer: It is an exact regression test for any implementation of the CAD fallback.

statements.statement: In fine-parameter space, failure of the odd-factor graph recursion is contained in \(\bigcup_{j\to i\in G}\{A_{ii}=A_{jj}=0\}\). For any fixed even diagonal-root branch, failure is contained in \(\bigcup_{j\to i\in G}\{A_{ii}=-A_{jj}\}\). Outside these proper algebraic sets, each diagonal branch produces at most one recursively determined \(A\) and at most one diagonal \(D\), after which the full \((B,Q)\) equations only filter branches.
statements.justification: The theorem promotes isolated examples to an algebraically generic identification-and-ambiguity phase diagram.
statements.gap: No cited subsampling paper identifies the exact graph-indexed exceptional varieties for target recovery.
statements.consumer: It supports diagnostics that route almost every compatible odd-factor input through a closed form and reserve CAD for named collision strata.

statements.statement: Uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{reg}}(d,m,G;\gamma,L,d_{\min},d_{\max},\kappa)\), \(\sqrt n\big((\widehat h_{uv}(z)-h_{uv}(z))_{z\in\mathcal Z}\big)\) converges to the centered Gaussian law obtained by applying the Jacobian of the moment-to-root recursion and \(\mathrm dh(z)=z\,\mathrm dA_{vu}/(1-A_{vv}z)+A_{vu}z^2\,\mathrm dA_{vv}/(1-A_{vv}z)^2\) to the long-run Gaussian lag-moment covariance. A consistent plug-in estimate of \(\Sigma_h\) yields simultaneous Wald bands over \(\mathcal Z\) with asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\).
statements.justification: The regular stratum should retain conventional efficient-looking uncertainty quantification rather than paying the cost of global set inversion everywhere.
statements.gap: Reiter et al. derive Wald laws from identified fine-grid coefficients; the additional root-map derivative and uniform branch-separation argument are absent there.
statements.consumer: Researchers with clearly separated odd-factor fits obtain familiar simultaneous frequency bands while using the exact certificate as a diagnostic.

statements.statement: There is an explicit expression for \(K_\Sigma=K_\Sigma(d,m,\gamma,L,d_{\max})\), obtained from the coarse spectral-density resolvent, such that for every \(n\ge3\), \(\Pr\{(M_0,M_1)\in\mathcal C_n^M(\alpha)\}\ge1-\alpha\) uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cmp}}(d,m,G;\gamma,L,d_{\min},d_{\max})\). One admissible calibration is certified by \(\|H_{\ell ij}\|_{\mathrm F}\le n^{-1/2}\), \(\|H_{\ell ij}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le n^{-1}\), Gaussian quadratic-form tails, and the radius \(r_n=2K_\Sigma\{\sqrt{\log(4d^2/\alpha)/n}+\log(4d^2/\alpha)/n\}\); verified rational outward rounding can only enlarge the region.
statements.justification: This closes the finite-sample calibration bottleneck needed for honest inference at singular and unidentified laws.
statements.gap: Basu and Michailidis control Gaussian Gram matrices, Hsu et al. control quadratic forms, and Giurcanu and Spokoiny give scalar covariance bands; none supplies this joint multivariate lag region with explicit compact-class constants and exact-computation rounding.
statements.consumer: Any branch-free transfer certificate can be inverted with advertised finite-sample coverage, including near root collisions where Wald approximations fail.

statements.statement: For every data-generating member of \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cmp}}(d,m,G;\gamma,L,d_{\min},d_{\max})\), \(\Pr\{h_{uv}\in\mathcal C_n^h\}\ge1-\alpha\). The claim holds without selecting a matrix-root branch and without divided-difference or branch-separation assumptions. At a nonidentified law the set need not contract, while at a regular identified law its local component has \(n^{-1/2}\) diameter.
statements.justification: Inverse-image coverage is the globally valid counterpart to local branchwise Wald inference.
statements.gap: The cited process-graph inference paper conditions on a differentiable fine-grid effect and does not cover observationally equivalent roots or singular fibers.
statements.consumer: Scientific conclusions remain valid when sampling parity, persistence collisions, or finite samples leave several fine-grid causal explanations alive.

statements.statement: Can the spectral-split adaptive calibration handle produce a rationally outward-rounded moment region that is coordinatewise no wider than the deterministic \(K_\Sigma\)-box with probability tending to one on every interior regular law, while retaining finite-sample coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) uniformly over the compact class and preserving exact semialgebraic inversion?
statements.justification: The fixed worst-case envelope may be conservative, and safe adaptivity is the main route to practically informative global sets.
statements.gap: Existing Gaussian covariance bands estimate variance locally, while the required dominance, uniform coverage, rational encoding, and multibranch inversion have not been combined.
statements.consumer: The answer determines whether globally honest transfer sets can be narrow enough for routine use without sacrificing validity at branch mergers.

statements.statement: If the observation scheme is specialized to \(m=1\), then \(B=A\), \(Q=D\), \(\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\) is either empty or the singleton \((B,Q)\), and the certificate returns \(h_{uv}(z)=B_{vu}z/(1-B_{vv}z)\), the standard unaliased direct process transfer.
statements.justification: This verifies that the new machinery collapses to the familiar fine-grid formula when aliasing is removed.
statements.gap: The reduction is not a novelty claim; it is the required fidelity check against standard process-graph transfer analysis.
statements.consumer: Implementers can test the certificate against an unaliased benchmark before using it on subsampled data.

sampling_model.design: A single stationary Gaussian fine-grid VAR(1) is observed systematically at times \(0,m,\ldots,nm\), with known \(m\) and supplied labeled process DAG \(G\).
sampling_model.units: The sampling units are the \(n+1\) dependent coarse-time vectors \((Y_0,\ldots,Y_n)\).
sampling_model.treatment: There is no binary treatment; the causal intervention is a unit perturbation transmitted along the direct process edge \(u\to v\).
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable; stability keeps \(1-A_{vv}z\ne0\) on \(\mathbb T\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate \((M_0,M_1)\) by overlapping empirical lag moments. On the regular odd stratum, map them through \((\widehat B,\widehat Q)\), the graph recursion, and the rational transfer. Globally, invert the outward-rounded moment box through all fine-grid branches.

estimand_functional: \(\mathcal H_{uv}(B,Q;G)=\{A_{vu}z/(1-A_{vv}z):(A,D)\in\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\}\), with \(\operatorname{Cert}_{uv,m,G}(B,Q)\) returning its unique element or two attained unequal elements

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Under the Gaussianity assumption of the data, the solutions are generally not unique.
We present a unifying framework for parameter identifiability and estimation under both subsampling and mixed frequencies when the shocks are non-Gaussian.
The algorithm forms a Schur decomposition and computes a \(p\)-th root of the triangular factor by a recursion.
The spectral latent-factor half-trek criterion identifies direct link functions by rational operations on the spectral density.
We characterise the asymptotic distribution of causal effect and spectral contribution estimators in terms of algebraic relations dictated by the process graph.
We establish useful deviation bounds for dependent Gaussian data using a spectral measure of stability.
We prove an exponential probability tail inequality for positive semidefinite quadratic forms in a subgaussian random vector.
The results about coverage probability are stated in a nonasymptotic way and apply for small and moderate sample size.
We provide a constraint satisfaction procedure for system-timescale causal structures corresponding to a measurement-timescale structure.
Classical CAD projection algorithms preserve chordal structure when projection follows a perfect elimination ordering.
In the regular mixed-frequency VARMA case with moving-average order exceeding autoregressive order, generic local identification fails.

tldr: Subsampling turns a fine-grid process DAG into a matrix-root problem, but causal identification depends on the entire root-and-innovation fiber rather than on one numerical root. The paper characterizes this fiber for ordered Gaussian VAR(1) systems: odd factors identify every transfer off explicit divided-difference collision varieties, even factors preserve an unavoidable global sign pair for every nonzero edge, and exact real-algebraic elimination returns either the common rational transfer or two attained same-law witnesses on all singular strata. A regular recursive estimator receives simultaneous Wald bands, while a finite-sample region for overlapping coarse lag moments is inverted through every branch to give globally honest transfer sets without post-selection.

project_justification.gap: Published subsampling results either invoke non-Gaussian shocks to identify the fine model, enumerate qualitative graph equivalence classes, or choose a numerical matrix-root branch. Published process-graph effect theory begins with fine-grid spectral information, and its Wald theory is local. No result decides a queried Gaussian transfer over the complete graph- and covariance-compatible root fiber.
project_justification.niche: A supplied causal order makes triangular root recursion available, while diagonal fine innovations make the coarse covariance an informative branch filter. Divided-difference zero sets isolate a small but essential singular problem that exact real algebraic methods can decide without pretending the parameter fiber is closed or finite.
project_justification.fill: The project gives a parity-sharp graph recursion, a universal even-factor same-law obstruction, a total transfer-aware CAD fallback with exact witnesses, local Wald bands on an explicit regular class, and finite-sample branch-free inversion of a rationally rounded coarse-moment region.

related_work: Gong et al. (2015) motivate causal-frequency recovery and prove non-Gaussian identification, while their Gaussian discussion supplies the broad nonuniqueness against which the parity certificate is positioned. Tank, Fox, and Shojaie (2019) also use non-Gaussian shocks and likelihood methods, so their information regime is complementary rather than a Gaussian comparator. Hyttinen et al. (2017) preserve qualitative subsampling ambiguity through exact constraints; the present target is a numerical rational transfer. Smith (2003), Bini, Higham, and Meini (2005), and Higham (2008) supply the triangular-root recursion and branch theory; the new content begins when graph zeros, the diagonal-innovation covariance equation, transfer equality, and complete fiber certification are imposed jointly. Reiter et al. (2026) identify rational link effects from the unaliased fine-grid spectrum, and Reiter et al. (2024) derive local delta-method inference once fine-grid coefficients are differentiably estimable. Basu and Michailidis (2015), Hsu, Kakade, and Zhang (2012), and Giurcanu and Spokoiny (2004) provide the concentration ingredients for a finite-sample lag-moment region. Li et al. (2023) and Wilson et al. (2014) inform the exact algebraic fallback but do not analyze this compatibility system. Deistler, Koelbl, and Anderson (2017), Anderson et al. (2016), and Gersing, Sögner, and Deistler (2023) show that mixed-frequency retrieval changes sharply across VAR, VARMA, and unit-root classes; those extensions are outside the present stationary VAR(1) scope.
technical_internal_limitation: The genericity claim is made in fine-parameter space, not in the image space of observed coarse laws. Exact CAD has worst-case doubly exponential complexity, and the proposal certifies termination rather than polynomial-time scalability. For arbitrary unnamed real inputs, Tarski--Seidenberg gives relative definability only; executable witness extraction requires an effective real closed field or verified rational input intervals. The Temperature--Ozone example in Gong et al. is used only as a conditional \(m=2\) Gaussian ambiguity audit if an external scientific argument supplies the one-way order; their fitted model does not establish that order.
honest_scope: The graph path expansion, parity zero sets, global even sign action, and singular two-node fiber have strong algebraic support but remain statements to prove in this proposal. The largest unresolved proof obligation is the explicit uniform calibration of the overlapping lag-moment region, including constants, stationary initialization, and verified outward rounding. The open adaptive-calibration question is not needed for baseline coverage. The paper does not claim point identification at odd-factor zero collisions, contraction at nonidentified laws, unknown-order recovery, unknown sampling-factor recovery, high-dimensional rates, or a practical worst-case CAD complexity bound. When \(m=1\), the construction reduces to the standard unaliased process transfer.

seed_details.anchor_read: Introduction, Section 3.2, Theorem 2 and its supplementary proof, and Section 6 were read. The proof identifies the mixing matrix from non-Gaussian innovations and leaves Gaussian second-order root multiplicity unresolved.
seed_details.question: For a supplied ordered process DAG and Gaussian shocks, characterize exactly when the direct transfer \(h_{uv}(z)\) is constant on the complete stable root-and-innovation fiber, with a graph recursion on regular strata and exact witnesses on singular strata.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace Gong et al.'s independent-component recovery of \([I,A,\ldots,A^{m-1}]\) by Smith's entrywise triangular-root recurrence, then retain every zero divided-difference stratum instead of selecting a root.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing subsampled Gaussian VARs with triangular roots, transfer functions, parity, and real quantifier elimination found matrix-root algorithms and broad nonidentification results, but no target-specific complete certificate.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: this is immediate from Gong et al. because their Theorem 2 already gives the odd-versus-even sign frontier. Rebuttal: their theorem uses non-Gaussian independent-component information, whereas this seed uses only the Gaussian coarse law, admits singular positive-dimensional fibers, filters roots by the coarse covariance, and certifies a transfer rather than the whole transition matrix.

seed_details.anchor_read: Introduction, Sections 2.2--2.3, Propositions 2.3--2.4 and their quadratic-form proof, and Section 7 were read. The paper controls Gaussian sample Gram matrices through a spectral-density envelope but does not invert a multibranch causal fiber.
seed_details.question: Can an explicit finite-sample simultaneous region for overlapping lag-zero and lag-one Gaussian moments be outward-rounded and inverted through the full root fiber to cover \(h_{uv}\) uniformly at branch collisions?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Represent both lag-zero and nonsymmetric lag-one entries as symmetric quadratic forms of one stacked Gaussian trajectory, rather than applying a sparse Gram-matrix bound only at lag zero.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for finite-sample multivariate lag-moment regions combined with semialgebraic root-fiber inversion found separate concentration and covariance-band results, but no branch-free causal-transfer inversion.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: union bounds and Hanson--Wright make this routine. Rebuttal: the load-bearing work is a common explicit covariance-operator envelope for overlapping lag products, exact rational outward rounding, and coverage-preserving inversion across singular and disconnected root fibers.

seed_details.anchor_read: Introduction, Propositions 3.2 and 4.2, the elimination-tree complexity discussion, and Section 7 were read. Chordality is preserved under a perfect elimination order, but the result is not specialized to path-filled VAR compatibility polynomials.
seed_details.question: Does ancestor closure in a supplied process DAG yield a perfect elimination order and a graph-height bound for the residual CAD problem after regular triangular coordinates are removed?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Compute the correlative-sparsity graph after expanding \(A^m\) and the accumulated covariance, because directed-path monomials create fill that is absent from the original DAG.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches combining chordal CAD, matrix powers, Lyapunov-type covariance equations, and subsampled causal graphs found no bound preserving exact witness extraction.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: Li et al.'s elimination-tree bound applies verbatim. Rebuttal: its premise concerns the polynomial correlative graph; proving that the powered-transition and accumulated-covariance system has controlled chordal completion is precisely the missing theorem.

seed_details.anchor_read: Introduction, Theorems 1 and 4, their identification argument, and the empirical discussion were read. Their recovery without a supplied order relies on independent non-Gaussian shocks.
seed_details.question: When is \(h_{uv}\) invariant across every permutation-triangular Gaussian root compatible with the coarse law?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace non-Gaussian column matching by a finite union over topological orders, with polynomial transfer-equality tests inside each order-root cell.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found complete qualitative graph enumeration under subsampling but no numerical transfer invariance over joint order and root uncertainty.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: enumerating \(d!\) orders and invoking CAD is only brute force. Rebuttal: a publishable version needs an order-invariance criterion or symmetry quotient; without it the seed is computationally correct but mathematically thin.

seed_details.anchor_read: Introduction, Theorems 1--3, the free-autocovariance construction, Theorem 6, and Section 5 were read. The paper proves generic parameter nonidentification for regular mixed-frequency VARMA models with moving-average order exceeding autoregressive order.
seed_details.question: Can an ordered graph make one rational process transfer constant along Deistler et al.'s free-autocovariance fiber even when the full VARMA parameter is not locally identified?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Differentiate the transfer along the paper's open autocovariance directions and characterize when its differential annihilates the fiber tangent space before applying global algebraic elimination.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing mixed-frequency VARMA nonidentification with target-specific process transfers found parameter-level retrieval and process-graph effect identification, but no functional refinement of the \(r>p\) boundary.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: a generic free parameter will generically change every nonconstant transfer. Rebuttal: graph zeros can make a rational target orthogonal to nuisance directions, but the seed lacks a concrete nondegenerate graph family after the deeper scan.

seed_details.anchor_read: Introduction, Sections 3.1--3.4, Theorem 1, its delta-method construction, and Section 6 were read. The paper derives Wald laws when the fine-grid SVAR effect is already a differentiable function of identified coefficients.
seed_details.question: Derive simultaneous Wald bands for \(h_{uv}\) after a smooth graph-recursive root map, with an explicit separation margin from divided-difference and branch collisions.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Compose the lag-moment central limit theorem with the implicit derivative of the selected triangular root before applying the rational effect derivative.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found local matrix-function perturbation theory and fine-grid process-effect Wald inference, but no inference after subsampling-root identification.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: this is a direct delta-method corollary of Reiter et al. Rebuttal: the root Jacobian and branch matching are new, but standing alone the result remains an inference appendix rather than the kernel.

seed_details.anchor_read: The Gaussian nonuniqueness discussion around Section 3.2 and the matrix-root examples were read together with the supplementary proof of Theorem 2.
seed_details.question: Characterize the topology and exact semialgebraic endpoints of transfer identified sets on zero divided-difference strata, distinguishing open pair fibers from attained transfer witnesses.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: At \(C_m(A_{vv},A_{uu})=0\), stop dividing and project the residual polynomial and covariance equations jointly onto \((A_{vu},A_{vv})\).
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found no treatment of open singular root fibers filtered by diagonal fine-grid innovation covariance.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: CAD automatically describes the set, so there is no theorem. Rebuttal: the nontrivial result is the target-aware equality test and attained two-witness certificate despite open or positive-dimensional parameter fibers.

seed_details.anchor_read: Introduction, the system-to-measurement graph map, the constraint formulation, experiments, and discussion were read. The paper allows an unknown subsampling rate for qualitative graph recovery.
seed_details.question: For \(m\) known only to lie in a finite set, decide whether \(h_{uv}\) is invariant over the union of all compatible factor-specific Gaussian fibers.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Enrich each discrete sampling-factor candidate with numerical matrix-power, covariance, stability, and transfer-equality constraints.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found unknown-rate graph compatibility but no functional certificate over numerical Gaussian root fibers.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: a finite union of already solved fixed-\(m\) certificates is immediate. Rebuttal: the cross-factor equality test is exact but does not supply enough new mathematics beyond the fixed-factor kernel.

seed_details.anchor_read: The non-Gaussian identifiability assumptions and complete SVAR identification theorem were read.
seed_details.question: Find the smallest quantified departure from Gaussianity that breaks the even global-sign transfer ambiguity, and derive a critical cumulant threshold for reliable branch discrimination.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace exact independent-component uniqueness by local testing between sign-paired innovation convolutions using the first nonzero odd cumulant.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found non-Gaussian exact identification and ICA perturbation results, but no observable critical threshold tailored to subsampling sign pairs.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: identifiability has no positive cumulant threshold at population level; any nonzero asymmetric cumulant may suffice. Rebuttal: a statistical detection boundary could exist, but that is a different local-asymptotic project and the proposed critical-\(\delta\) object was not yet defensible.

seed_details.anchor_read: Introduction, the blocked differencing construction, the generic identification theorem, and the conclusion were read. The paper identifies unit-root VAR parameters from mixed-frequency second moments after lagged differencing.
seed_details.question: Can cointegrating graph restrictions identify a stationary long-run causal transfer when the fine transition has a unit root and observations are subsampled?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Apply graph recursion to the stable block after the paper's lag-\(N\) differencing and isolate the unit-root block through the cointegrating decomposition.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found unit-root parameter retrieval and stationary process-graph effects separately, but no parity certificate for cointegrating transfers.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: the target \(A_{vu}z/(1-A_{vv}z)\) is singular at the unit root and is not the right long-run estimand. Rebuttal: a cointegrating transfer can be defined, but doing so changes the target beyond the present brief.

surviving_candidates.occupation_check: The exact Gaussian target-method pair is unoccupied: triangular root recursion is published, but complete transfer constancy over the graph- and covariance-filtered fiber is not.
Finite-sample quadratic-form control and local fine-grid Wald inference are occupied separately; rationally rounded joint lag-moment inversion across every compatible root branch is not.

adjacent_threads.settled: Gong et al. and Tank, Fox, and Shojaie obtain fine-grid recovery from non-Gaussian innovation information under their respective structural conditions; Hyttinen et al. enumerate compatible qualitative system-timescale graphs.
adjacent_threads.unsettled: None gives a sound-and-complete numerical certificate for whether one Gaussian fine-grid transfer is constant over every stable root satisfying the coarse innovation equation.

adjacent_threads.settled: Classical Schur methods recursively compute a selected triangular \(m\)-th root and analyze branch choice and numerical stability.
adjacent_threads.unsettled: They do not impose a process DAG and diagonal fine innovations, project the entire compatible fiber onto a causal transfer, or return same-law ambiguity witnesses.

adjacent_threads.settled: Rational frequency-domain link effects can be identified from an unaliased fine-grid spectrum under graphical criteria, and differentiable fine-grid estimators admit delta-method Wald laws.
adjacent_threads.unsettled: The fine spectrum is unavailable under subsampling, and local Wald theory does not protect root collisions or observationally equivalent branches.

adjacent_threads.settled: Spectral envelopes bound finite-trajectory covariance operators; quadratic-form tails and nonasymptotic scalar covariance intervals are available.
adjacent_threads.unsettled: The papers do not combine overlapping multivariate lag-zero and lag-one moments, rational outward rounding, and global inversion through a semialgebraic causal fiber.

adjacent_threads.settled: CAD is complete over effectively represented real closed fields, and chordal or variety-restricted variants can reduce unnecessary projection and lifting.
adjacent_threads.unsettled: No existing result identifies the sparse elimination structure or complete witness contract for the powered-transition and accumulated-covariance equations.

literature_map.closest_non_subsumption: Smith's recursion covers the regular algebraic step but not the causal compatible-law fiber. Gong et al.'s parity conclusion is powered by non-Gaussian mixing information, not by Gaussian coarse moments with a supplied order. Reiter et al. begin with the fine-grid spectrum. The conjunction of covariance filtering, singular-fiber completeness, transfer rather than parameter equality, and global branch-free inference is therefore not subsumed by the closest papers.

novelty_justification: The closest identification comparator is Gong et al. (2015), which states general Gaussian nonuniqueness and proves recovery by non-Gaussian independent-component information. The closest algebraic comparator is Smith (2003), which computes one triangular matrix root recursively. The proposed kernel instead characterizes a target-specific Gaussian observational fiber after a supplied process DAG and the coarse innovation covariance are imposed: odd regular strata have a unique graph-recursive transfer, every even factor retains a global sign-paired ambiguity for a nonzero edge, and singular strata receive a terminating complete transfer-equality decision with attained witnesses. The inference layer is also distinct from Reiter et al. (2024): it inverts a finite-sample coarse-moment region across all branches and singularities rather than conditioning on a differentiable identified fine-grid parameter.
